sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 3.16(ii), p.55, and Theorem A(ii), p.4, in the published version, Inventiones mathematicae 222 (2020), 1–77 (author-hosted copy with journal pagination, SHA-256 daeb43ec…46a9)
sourceIssues.printed: Theorem A: "Let X be a smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible real variety, of dimension d ≥ 1. Assume that X satisfies the real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles and that H²(X, O_X) = 0. … (ii) There exists a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus in X if and only if the natural map Pic(X)[2^∞] → Pic(X_C)^G[2^∞] is onto." Theorem 3.16 assumes "dim(X) > 0".
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis d ≥ 2 (or X(R) = ∅); the proof, which goes through Proposition 3.9, needs d ≥ 2 when X(R) ≠ ∅.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample in dimension one: X = E, the real elliptic curve y² = x³ − x. Here H²(E, O_E) = 0 and the Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles (codimension 0) holds. The only geometrically irreducible curve in E is E itself, of geometric genus 1, so the left side fails. Since E(R) ≠ ∅, Br(R) → Br(E) is injective and Pic(E) → Pic(E_C)^G is an isomorphism, so the right side holds. Proposition 3.9 (a curve of odd geometric genus exists) is stated for dimension ≥ 2, as the introduction says (p.4). The surface and higher-dimensional cases, which are the paper's applications, are unaffected. Found by the extraction (items printed-even-genus, main-even-genus).

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, paragraph before Example 2.5, p.37, in the published version, Inventiones mathematicae 222 (2020), 1–77 (author-hosted copy with journal pagination, SHA-256 daeb43ec…46a9)
sourceIssues.printed: "Namely, let X be a smooth and proper variety over a real closed field R and let k ≥ 0 be even, so that Z(2k) = Z(k). We can view ω^{2k} … as an element of H^{2k}_G(X(C), Z(k)). This class is Hodge if R = R, being torsion, and it belongs to H^{2k}_G(X(C), Z(k))_0 if (and only if) X(R) = ∅."
sourceIssues.reason: For k = 0, ω^0 = 1 is not torsion, and it is the class of X itself, hence algebraic and in the subgroup cut out by the topological condition even when X(R) ≠ ∅; the "if and only if" fails. For even k > 0 the statement is as printed. Noted by the extraction (item constant-omega).
